Hi Mathilde, Takahiro —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. As discussed, we want to run a small cross-border pilot with EvoSI (France) and ZenCloud (JP) to validate:

- Local SI deployment patterns for customer-managed data flows
- Data residency enforcement at region boundary (EU and JP)
- Runtime performance with prefix/KV caching when data residency is enforced

Attached is a 1-pager scope and a proposed timeline (pilot-scope.xlsx). High-level asks:

1) Partners: confirm resource leads, brief delivery windows (2-week sprints)
2) Redwood: provide a test tenant and an initial DPA and data-flow diagram
3) Compliance check: verify encryption in-transit/rest, key management options (bring-your-own-key)

Can each partner reply with a short confirmation and the name of the engineer assigned? From Redwood side Ill coordinate legal/compliance (cc Sergio) and runtime questions (cc Hiro).

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan

Thanks Priya — quick technical notes from runtime:

- Model serving and KV/prefix cache must not leak cross-region keys. For the pilot we will:
  * Run region-isolated inference clusters (one per region)
  * Ensure KV cache persisted only in-region or encrypted with region-scoped keys
- Bring-your-own-key flows: we support customer KMS integration but need partner help for KMS network peering (if on-prem)
- Network: if partners plan to host inference in partner-managed VPCs, we need VPC peering details and a testing window for MTU and throughput (30-60 min bench)

Action items for partners:
- Confirm whether the partner-hosted clusters will be in partner VPCs or on Redwood Dedicated (we can provide dedicated nodes if needed)
- Provide contact for your infra engineer to coordinate KMS/peering details

I'll attach a sketch of the recommended data-flow and where the tokenization/kv/cache boundaries will be (see data-flow-diagram.png).

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

From a compliance standpoint, checklist items for the pilot:

- DPA execution: Redwood will provide an initial DPA (attached DPA_draft_redwood_v1.pdf). EvoSI legal has indicated 3–5 business days for review.
- Data classification: partners to label test dataset (we need 'personal' vs 'synthetic')
- Key management: confirm whether partners will bring KMS or use Redwood-managed keys; if BYOK, provide KMS endpoints and key IDs
- Audit logs & retention: pilot will require 30-day retention of request logs; Redwood can export logs to partner S3/GCS buckets behind presigned URLs
- Security scanning: quick dependency scan on partner deployment artifacts before first run

Please note: any full production rollout will require SOC2 evidence and penetration test results — not needed for the pilot but noted for timeline.

Attachments: DPA_draft_redwood_v1.pdf
